text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Nightspot owners whose premises are found with illegal drugs, including Ecstacy pills, will be charged with drug trafficking, said Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayub.
-- Employers who retrench local workers and employ foreign workers in their place will be subjected to severe fines once the Empoyment Act 1955 is amended, said Human Resource Minister Lim Ah Lek.

-- Renong Bhd has won a contract for construction of the 625 million ringgit Bangalore to Mysore highway in India, said Works Minister S. Samy Vellu. Two other Malaysian companies also look set to win other contracts, he said.

-- Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid expressed disappointment that only 5,000 illegal immigrants had responded to the government's amnesty for surrendering themselves. Around one million illegal foreigners remain in the country.

-- The Swansea Institute of Higher Education is reviewing its courses run in Malaysia after allegations that 500 certificates for post-graduate diplomas bearing the institute's seal had been printed in Malaysia.
